column1: # Labels for platform methods real apps call: what each returns, as the privacy API model's classes.
# Made from the API corpus of 28 F-Droid apps (scripts/ml/app_api_corpus.py; apps and hashes in
# benchmarks/privacy/apps/apps.tsv), reviewed on 2026-10-14 against the Android SDK reference and its
# RequiresPermission annotations. Not derived from SuSi or FlowDroid, so the model trained without
# them is measured independently on them (scripts/ml/evaluate_api_model.py).
# Rules. A source returns personal data the app did not pass in: what a method returns when called on
# platform objects (Location.getLatitude on the device's fix). source:location: positions, movement,
# addresses, the serving cell's identity. Fix metadata (time, accuracy, provider), satellite status,
# signal strength, channel and operator codes, physical cell ids: none. source:other: personal data
# outside the privacy map's kinds (clipboard, installed apps, nearby and paired devices, screen and
# typed text read by accessibility services and keyboards, system logs, the browsing URL). Handles,
# factories, builders and pure functions of the arguments (a URI or phone-number formatter): none.
# Generic accessors whose argument decides (Settings.Secure.getString, ExifInterface.getAttribute,
# ContentResolver.query): none; the privacy map handles them by argument. Methods of personal-data
# classes were reviewed one by one; the model's confident source predictions elsewhere by package,
# with every name suggesting personal data reviewed one by one.
